title: Universal base open with local-complete-intersection fibres for a flat closed family
statement: Algebraic spaces and their etale scheme charts are as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], with the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention] and underlying point topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Flatness and local finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts by [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Fibre products of algebraic spaces use [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], agreeing on schemes with [def-pc-fibre-product]. For a point $s$ of the scheme base, a geometric fibre is $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\overline{\kappa(s)}$, with the field and geometric-point conventions of [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. A scheme over a field is a local complete intersection if it has an affine open cover by spectra of finitely generated local-complete-intersection algebras [def-weil-pbc-complete-intersection-over-field]; for an algebraic space over a field this condition is tested on etale scheme charts. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $f:X\to S$ be a flat locally finitely presented morphism of algebraic spaces whose underlying map $|X|\to|S|$ is closed. There exists an open subscheme $W_f\subseteq S$ such that for every scheme morphism $g:T\to S$, $g$ factors through $W_f$ if and only if every fibre of $X\times_ST\to T$ is a local complete intersection over its residue field. Formation of $W_f$ commutes with arbitrary base change between schemes. Equivalently, $s\in W_f$ if and only if $X_s$ is a local complete intersection over $\kappa(s)$; the same condition can be checked on a geometric fibre. No dimension, properness, connectedness, or nonemptiness assumption is made.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-fibrewise-lci-source-locus] to the given flat locally finitely presented $f$. Write $U=U_f$, and $B=|X|\setminus|U|$. Thus $B$ is closed. For every scheme base change $T\to S$, its inverse image $B_T$ is the complement of $|U_{f_T}|$ in $|X_T|$. The same cited statement gives $B_T=\varnothing$ if and only if all fibres of $f_T$ are local complete intersections. In particular, this criterion applies when $T$ is the spectrum of a residue field or of an algebraically closed extension of it.

Since the underlying map $|f|$ is closed by hypothesis, $C=|f|(B)$ is a closed subset of $|S|$. Put $W=|S|\setminus C$ and give $W$ the open subscheme structure obtained by restricting the structure sheaf of $S$. By construction $s\in W$ exactly when no point of $B$ lies above $s$. This uses only the given closed-map hypothesis and the definition of an open subscheme [def-pc-scheme].

Fix a scheme morphism $g:T\to S$, put $X_T=X\times_ST$, and denote its projections by $h:X_T\to X$ and $f_T:X_T\to T$. We claim $|f_T|(B_T)=|g|^{-1}(C)$. The inclusion from left to right follows by projecting a point of $B_T=h^{-1}(B)$. Conversely let $t\in T$ have image $s\in C$, and choose $x\in B$ above $s$. Take a surjective etale scheme atlas $a:V\to X$ from [def-trf-algebraic-space], and a point $v\in V$ above $x$. Apply [lem-a1-space-fibre-product-point] to the scheme maps $V\to S$ and $T\to S$ and the points $v,t$. It gives a point of $V\times_ST$ over $v,t$, represented after a common field extension; its projections still have the original underlying points $v,t$. The morphism $V\times_ST\to X_T$ supplied by the fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] sends this point to some $x_T$ over $x,t$. Since $x\in B$, we have $x_T\in h^{-1}(B)=B_T$. Thus $t\in|f_T|(B_T)$, proving the reverse inclusion.

By step 3, $B_T$ is empty exactly when $|g|(T)\subseteq W$. Indeed a set is empty if and only if its image under a function is empty. The latter containment is equivalent to factorization of $g$ through the open subscheme $W$: by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product], the pullback $T\times_SW$ is the open subscheme $g^{-1}(W)$ of $T$; it equals $T$ exactly under that containment, yielding the required factorization, and any factorization gives the containment. Combining this with step 1 proves the stated universal property for all scheme morphisms $g$.

For any $g:T\to S$, define the subset $W_T=|T|\setminus|f_T|(B_T)$. Step 3 gives $W_T=g^{-1}(W)$, so it is open even though $f_T$ need not be closed. Its open subscheme is $W\times_ST$ by [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product]. For every further scheme map $R\to T$, composition with $g$ and step 4 show that it factors through this open exactly when all fibres of $X\times_SR\to R$ are local complete intersections. By the fibre-product universal property [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], this family is $X_T\times_TR\to R$. Thus $W_T$ has the required universal property for the base-changed family. Uniqueness follows by applying the universal properties of two candidate opens to their own inclusions into the base. Consequently formation of the universal open commutes with arbitrary scheme base change.

Take $T=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ in step 4. Its map to $S$ factors through $W$ exactly when $s\in W$, while its family has just the fibre $X_s$; hence $s\in W$ if and only if $X_s$ is a local complete intersection. Taking instead $T=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ for any algebraically closed field extension $\Omega/\kappa(s)$ gives the same image point $s$ and the geometric fibre $X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Step 4 therefore gives the equivalent geometric-fibre criterion, with no separability restriction. If $X_s$ is empty, the fibre condition is vacuous and $s\in W$, exactly as the complement construction prescribes. If $X$ is empty then $B=C=\varnothing$ and $W=S$.

This changes only the cited construction, with no change of hypotheses, conclusions or proof route.
